articles.title: Decolonizing perceptions about Africa
articles.summary: A UN resolution to redraw the global map to project the African continent more accurately, national initiatives to decolonize schools and a campaign to present positive developments are changing the…

image.caption: Artists are among the Africans on the continent and in the diaspora presenting a more varied image of Africa Image: DW

blocks.text: The Correct the Map resolution to promote map projections that more realistically reflect the true size of continents endorsed by the United Nations in New York at the beginning of September was a huge success for the African countries that led the campaign. In the General Assembly, 164 member states voted to encourage the use of Equal Earth projection and other equal-area maps instead of the 16th-century Mercator projection.
Robert Dussey, the foreign minister of Togo, which sponsored the Correct the Map campaign at the UN, spoke of a "feeling of pride."
Correct the Map is also supported by the African Union.

"Finally, Africa is fighting to regain its place in the community of nations," he told DW. "The place it has been reserved to this day is unfair. It does not correspond to Africa's reality, not in historical, geographical or economic terms."

Dussey made clear that the debate about global maps was also clearly about symbolically redrawing the maps of facts and knowledge, culture and identity and redressing misperceptions about political and economic realities and power.
Trump's US only state to reject UN resolution

The only UN member state that rejected the resolution was the United States, whose president Donald Trump has engaged in various acts of political symbolism, having issued orders for places to be renamed on maps which he would presumaby also like to redraw Trump has signed executive orders to rename the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America, and Lake Ontario as Lake America.
The UN resolution, meanwhile, is part of a broader, global trend, as French historian Romain Tiquet from the African Worlds Institute (IMAF) told DW.

"Since the late 2000s and early 2010s, there has been a great deal of debate about the decolonization of knowledge — in universities, museums and cultural institutions, as well as within social movements and civil society."

He said many questions were being explored: "Who established the categories through which we conceptualize the world? From which locations? And what power dynamics result from this? And cartography fits right into this context."

blocks.caption: The Equal Earth map is aimed at a more accurate representation of the world Image: Equal Earth/Handout/AFP

blocks.text: Mali breaks with former colonial power France
Many African states have also been trying to free the school systems from colonial influence, often for political reasons.

In October 2025, the Malian government decided to remove French history from the school curriculum. The decision was made to stop teaching about the French Revolution but to focus on Malian history and the other ancient West African kingdoms.

In just a few years, the country's military government has made a clean break with the former colonial power. Mali ended its military cooperation with France in 2022, and French soldiers began to withdraw from the country. Burkina Faso and Niger did the same and the three formed the Alliance of Sahel States in 2023.

Philemon Mtoi from Tumaini University Makumira in Tanzania said Mali had made an important step: "As a historian, I believe that a country without a strong understanding of its own history is like a country without clear leadership and direction. This decision is important because it seeks to strengthen patriotism and foster a stronger sense of national identity."
By investing in the research and preservation of African history, Mali — like Africa as a whole — was making a strong contribution to global scholarship, Mtoi explained.

He spoke of "reclaiming and documenting African histories from an African perspective" and said that this was not only "an act of decolonization" but also an "important step toward intellectual independence."

Mtoi said that many other African countries, such as Ghana, Namibia, South Africa and Kenya, had adopted a similar approach. He added that his own country, Tanzania, had also made major changes to the school curriculum recently. He said that "Tanzanian history and ethics" was now a compulsory subject that had replaced global history and that it would be taught in Swahili, the country's national language.

The historian warned, however, that knowledge of other countries and histories should not be erased. He said it was important to acquire a profound knowledge of significant events in global history, such as the French Revolution, but that this could be done at a later stage.
How German merchants shaped Africa's fate
#NotWaiting campaign to abolish stereotypes

School education in a formal setting is only one part of the puzzle. The non-profit Africa No Filter was one of the organizations behind the Correct the Map campaign. It works to challenge and change harmful narratives about Africa.

In a report titled "The cost of media stereotypes to Africa," it says that "Africa could be losing up to $4.2 billion (€3.6 billion) annually in inflated interest payments due to biased media coverage."

Francois Bouda, an officer for arts and culture at Africa No Filter, said that media outlets continued to portray Africa as being poor, corrupt and crisis-ridden. The new campaign #NotWaiting is meant to change this perception.

"We are addressing Africans because we, too, need to change the way we view the African continent. We've accepted the image of a continent incapable of taking care of itself, one that is poor and has no opportunities. We've internalized this and come to believe it, even though many positive things are happening. First of all there has to be an internal change," said Bouda.
How the Berlin Conference spurred the colonization of Africa
'Millions of ordinary people doing extraordinary things every day'
The #NotWaiting campaign is part of a larger movement, which aims to highlight positive developments and initiatives in Africa, to focus on political programs and actors, to counter crisis-reporting.
It comprises figures on the continent and in the diaspora, people who are "not waiting for an external hand to dictate what path to follow," said Bouda.
"This is good for Africans," he said, adding that there were many actors but that the only problem was that they "aren't visible."

The campaign is about Africans themselves painting a positive picture of Africa as a continent on the move, about people sharing stories, which are not curated by international institutions or media outlets.

"We've been building all along," says a video clip to promote the campaign. "From village roads to crowded cities, across the 54 countries that make up the continent, millions of ordinary people doing extraordinary things every day."
This article, to which Sandrine Blanchard and Jean-Claude Abalo contributed, was originally written in German.

articles.title: CICC appeals to tech experts, hacking communities to protect youth from dark web dangers
articles.summary: The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) has appealed to various information and communications technology (ICT) and hacking communities to collaborate with the government in…

blocks.text: September 20, 2026 | 2:22pm
Police forensic experts sift through the scene of the deadly gun rampage on Sept. 18, 2026, inside a school campus in Banga, South Cotabato.
Philstar.com / John Unson

MANILA, Philippines — The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) has appealed to various information and communications technology (ICT) and hacking communities to collaborate with the government in protecting Filipino youth from the dangers of the dark web and preventing further tragic incidents.

In a DZBB interview on Sunday, September 20, CICC Executive Director Undersecretary Renato Paraiso acknowledged that the government has limitations in its current capabilities and urged tech-savvy individuals to step forward and help bridge these gaps.

"Sa ating mga kapatid, sa ating mga kasamahan, sa ating mga kaibigan sa mga iba't-ibang mga ICT communities, hacking communities, computer forums, kung may alam kayo or may access dito, mag-come forward kayo," Paraiso said.

(To our brothers and sisters, to our colleagues, to our friends in various ICT communities, hacking communities, and computer forums, if you know anything or have access to this, please come forward.)
"Magtulong-tulong tayo para sa ating mga kabataan. Please come forward. We don't need another incident like this, not at the expense of another child's life,” he added.
(Let’s help each other for the youth. Please come forward. We don't need another incident like this, not at the expense of another child's life.)

The appeal comes amid rising concerns over the "dark web," a hidden layer of the internet that is inaccessible through standard web browsers and requires specialized applications, skills and knowledge to access.
According to Paraiso, these underground forums serve as platforms where hacking communities, illegal firearms sellers and anonymous groups interact

Penetrating these exclusive online spaces to monitor potential threats is highly difficult. Paraiso explained that while surface-level monitoring tools are available, deeper intelligence work is necessary because gaining the credentials and trust required to enter these forums can take years.
“More importantly, the intelligence work that needs to go behind it kasi it takes years before you get credentials para pagkatiwalaan ka to be let inside these forums or communities, Paraiso said.
(More importantly, the intelligence work that needs to go behind it, because it takes years before you get credentials to be trusted enough to be let inside these forums or communities.)

On September 19, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said that the 14-year-old student who opened fire at a school in South Cotabato was heavily involved in activities on the “deep dark web.” The shooting incident left three people dead, including the shooter.
“Upon investigation, he was heavily into the deep dark web. He was into the deep dark web, which influenced him,” Remulla said in a press briefing on Saturday, September 19.
“According to his phone, he left several notes detailing his depression at tuloy-tuloy ito,” he added.

articles.title: Caucus on VP Sara Duterte impeachment voting threshold expected Monday --Ejercito
articles.summary: Senator-judges are expected to have a meeting on Monday regarding the voting threshold needed to either convict or acquit Vice President Sara Duterte in her impeachment trial, according to Senator JV…

blocks.text: Published September 20, 2026 2:19pm

Senator-judges are expected to have a meeting on Monday regarding the voting threshold needed to either convict or acquit Vice President Sara Duterte in her impeachment trial, according to Senator JV Ejercito.

"Malamang may caucus bukas [ukol sa isyu ng voting threshold]. Siguro pag-uusapan kung pagbobotohan ito o 'yung presiding officer na lang through our consesus," Ejercito told Super Radyo dzBB on Sunday.

(There will likely be a caucus on Monday regarding the issue of the voting threshold. Perhaps we will discuss whether this should be put to a vote or whether the presiding officer can decide through consensus.)

Earlier this week, senator-judges had asked amici curiae — former Supreme Court (SC) chief justices Artemio Panganiban, Hilario Davide, and Reynato Puno, and retired Associate Justice Adolf Azcuna — for their insights on whether the senators that are detained, on the run and those abroad should be included in the voting to impeach or acquit Duterte.
Panganiban, Davide, and Puno said the Senate impeachment court can change the 16-vote threshold for conviction, adding that the Senate has authority to try and decide impeachment cases.

They said the constitutional voting threshold required to convict an impeachable official should be based on the number of senator-judges who actively participated in the impeachment trial of Duterte.

However, Azcuna, one of the framers of the 1987 Constitution, offered a different view that the two-thirds concurrence requirement should relate to the entire membership of the Senate, hence a conviction by 16 senator-judges is needed.

Currently, Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta are detained over separate plunder charges, Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa is in hiding amid an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court, and Senator Loren Legarda has been on leave for weeks due to health concerns, and is currently abroad. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Hundreds of drones target Moscow on last day of voting in Russia’s parliamentary election
articles.summary:
Authorities accuse Ukraine of trying to disrupt poll and say 1,600 drones in total intercepted, while at least two people killed and oil refinery damaged

Hundreds of drones targeting Moscow…

blocks.text: Hundreds of drones targeting Moscow and its surrounding region killed at least two people and damaged a major refinery on the final day of the country’s parliamentary elections, authorities said on Sunday.
The capital’s mayor said that more than 1,600 drones had been intercepted and shot down, 450 of which were aimed at Moscow.
Sergei Sobyanin accused Ukraine of attempting to interfere with a tightly controlled three-day election that is set to tighten president Vladimir Putin’s 26-year grip on power.
“The unprecedented attack was clearly planned with the aim of disrupting the elections. The enemy did not succeed,” he said on Telegram.
Moscow’s regional governor said at least two people were killed – a 44-year-old woman and an elderly man – in two separate locations.
A fire triggered by a drone crashing into a 21-storey building also led to 400 people being evacuated, said Moscow regional governor, Andrey Vorobyov, without specifying the drones’ origin.

The attacks come at a time when Kyiv stepped up its long-range drone strike campaign against Russia in recent months, particularly against energy infrastructure to target a vital source of the Kremlin’s revenue to fund its war effort – now in its fifth year.

Ukrainian ​strikes have knocked out a significant part of Russia’s oil refining capacity, triggering oil product shortages, fuel price increases and long queues at filling stations in many regions across the country’s 11 time zones.
A facility on the territory of the Moscow oil refinery had been damaged, Sobyanin said. No casualties had been reported so far and emergency services were on the scene.
That major refinery has already been hit by Ukrainian strikes in recent months.
Ukraine has not commented on the attacks. Both sides ​say they do not ‌target civilians.
The latest strike comes after the US president, Donald Trump, said on Monday that Ukraine and Russia had agreed not to target each other’s energy facilities.
It also comes after Russians began voting on Friday in the country’s first parliamentary election since Moscow invaded Ukraine in February 2022.
Only parties that support Putin and the Kremlin’s military campaign have been registered to run. Moscow has also organised voting in occupied Ukraine.
Few Russians doubt Putin’s United Russia party will coast to victory again, but the vote offers a gauge of public support for the war.
With Agence France-Presse and Reuters

articles.title: Why China is pushing back on US warnings over rapid AI development
articles.summary:
Beijing believes slowdown calls aim to lock in US advantage, and is pursuing a different balance between safety and pace

About two years ago, education entrepreneur Boris But had what he…

blocks.text: About two years ago, education entrepreneur Boris But had what he calls a “penny-drop moment” – that, like countless others in China, his company needed to embrace AI before it was made obsolete by it.
His clients, well-off parents looking to send their children to study overseas, had begun arriving in his office reeling off information and opinions gleaned not from rival firms, but from chatbots.
In response, he started developing his own AI study tool, concluding: “If you can’t beat them, join them.”
The pace and quality of AI development in China is second only to the United States, with the two superpowers locked in an intensifying rivalry as the stakes rise with each new model’s capabilities.
Analysts generally agree that frontier, or cutting-edge, US models are still some way ahead of their Chinese counterparts.

But over the last few weeks the mood music from Silicon Valley has been decidedly sombre, as insider after insider has warned of the potential catastrophes that could result from “loss of control” of the most advanced AIs.
And last Saturday Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei pitched a “worldwide pacing of the frontier” – something he said would “require cooperation with China”.
“China is definitely not receptive” to a slowdown on US firms’ terms, though, said Lian Jye Su from technology research group Omdia.
For the government, AI is a “core sovereignty capability”, and Beijing will not want to jeopardise the progress made in closing the gap with US frontier models.
“It sees these calls [for a slowdown] as a bid to lock in US advantage,” said Su.
Amodei made this explicit, mentioning China specifically when arguing it was key “to keep democracies’ AI lead over autocracies as large as possible”.
He advocated for measures including continued export controls to China on advanced chips and machinery – the existence of which some argue already amounts to a forced unilateral “pacing”.
China’s foreign ministry responded to Amodei’s piece by saying “fearmongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only disrupt the process of global AI governance”.
However, several analysts told the Guardian it would be a mistake to assume this suggested a rejection of the broader concerns raised by the essay.

This week China released the third iteration of its AI safety governance framework – a document that functions as a “mapping of the AI risk landscape and roughly what one should do about it”, said Gabriel Wagner, a researcher at Concordia, a Beijing-based AI safety consultancy.

Included in the updates are the risks posed by agents, the cybersecurity threats from frontier models and the issue of recursive self-improvement – an as-yet hypothetical scenario where AI becomes advanced enough to improve itself.
“In many ways, I think there is more common ground than people might assume between what Amodei is saying and what the Chinese government is saying,” said Wagner.
That contrasts with US president Donald Trump, who this week called fears AI could wipe out humanity a “hoax”.
Trump is set to meet counterpart Xi Jinping in Washington next week, with AI expected to make the agenda, though analysts are sceptical a major breakthrough will happen.
The ruling Communist party, finely attuned to risks to its political control, has been proactive in ensuring the new technology has developed within boundaries set by the state.
Centralised authority over critical infrastructure and commercial activity means China is generally better placed than the United States “to address any AI disaster”, said Omdia’s Su.
However, Chinese companies do less voluntary monitoring and evaluation work than US ones, said Leia Wang from the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace (CEIP).
Neither government seems prepared for a loss-of-control incident like those outlined over the last few weeks, she said.
China’s regulation, though, is “iterative … they are quick to adapt and release new measures”, she added.
China has had an algorithm registry since 2022, but warnings on agents released this year suggest a switch in focus “from controlling what AI says to controlling what it does”, per Concordia AI.
Beijing also issued national regulations this year aimed at curbing emotional dependency on companion AIs.
At the same time, AI is being actively encouraged across the economy to promote growth, enshrining this goal in its latest Five Year Plan.

Local governments are offering funding and low rents to companies to help achieve this – entrepreneur But was recently invited to pitch his company, Hampshire Education, to a small city three hours from Shanghai set on establishing a reputation as a tech hub.
Factories across the country’s huge manufacturing base are being encouraged to convert their processes into the AI era.

“Safety and controllability are certainly major concerns, and they are actively discussed,” said a spokesperson for Black Lake Technologies, an industrial agent platform that says it has worked with 40,000 factories globally.
“But in manufacturing, these concerns tend to be much more concrete and operational … what companies care most about is whether the AI is reliable.”
Daily life in China is already highly digitised, with traditionally less discourse around data privacy helping with widespread adoption.
For example, digital health service A-fu, which features AI chatbot versions of prominent doctors trained on real clinical studies, recently hit 150 million users.
“Most people treat AI as an already-useful everyday tool, not an abstract threat, so the practical attitude is to live with it,” said Ni Tao, founding editor of tech website yangtzeer.com.
“There is real anxiety about jobs and misinformation, but it coexists with a strong belief that China must master AI rather than slow down.”

articles.title: How to know if you can trust an AI’s answer to your question
articles.summary: It might be useful to sort AI answers into an ‘answer typography’ of four broad types: factual, interpretive, constructive, and strategic

blocks.text: I recently typed a simple question into Google search: How much screen time is too much for teenagers? Instead of presenting links, as Google had been doing for many years, it gave me an AI-generated answer.

The artificial intelligence agent cited a number, then complicated that reply, noting that quality and balance of time could matter more than the number of hours, and that “too much” time could depend on a teenager’s sleep, exercise, school demands and mood.

I tried another search: Should I take a daily aspirin? This time the AI answer presented me with medical information, warned about risks and offered more tailored guidance if I provided my age and medical history.
These were good replies. What interested me was that they were different kinds of replies.
Debate about AI answers has focused on accuracy: Did the system get the answer right? That matters, but accuracy is only one test. Each kind of answer requires a user to judge something different.
I find it useful to sort AI answers into an “answer typography” of four broad types: factual, interpretive, constructive, and strategic.

A factual claim can often be checked against a source. An interpretation can be accurate and still reflect choices about which evidence matters. A construction can be well reasoned and still be wrong for the person receiving it. A beautifully written strategic document may not be true. Yet AI presents all four types of answers in much the same fluent, authoritative form; the differences are easy to miss.

I’m university librarian and dean of libraries at the University of Virginia who leads national efforts to develop AI competencies for library professionals, and I consult widely on AI literacy. I first proposed the typography in the Journal of Academic Librarianship.

The four categories are not airtight boxes. A response from an AI agent can reflect several types. That said, I describe each type of answer below, and offer guidance for deciding whether a reply is ready to use or needs more investigation.
A factual answer makes a claim that can, in principle, be checked against evidence. When was the University of Virginia founded? What is the chemical symbol for gold?

To determine whether a factual answer is robust enough for you to use, verify the claim against an appropriate source. If the answer cites a source, follow that link instead of simply treating the answer itself as proof.

An interpretive reply is built on evidence, but there is not a single takeaway. How much screen time is too much for a teenager? Does remote work raise productivity? The answer depends on what evidence is included, what is left out and how disagreement is understood.

Google’s initial answer to my screen-time question indicated that two hours was a limit for teenagers. Then it noted that pediatric guidance puts more weight on the quality and context of screen use than on simple hours. The American Academy of Pediatrics says there is no exact recommended amount for teens and emphasizes the kind of screen use and what activities it might be displacing. A question that looked numerical turned out to require interpretation.

To assess interpretive answers, do more than check facts. Ask yourself what evidence the system emphasized, what it left out and whether another defensible interpretation exists. A useful follow-up question to present to the search engine is: “What is the strongest evidence for a different conclusion?”
Constructive answers are made rather than discovered. Ask AI to draft a cover letter, write a eulogy, suggest a lesson plan or reorganize a paragraph — there is no single correct result.

You can judge the response by considering purpose, audience and voice. A eulogy can be grammatically perfect and still sound nothing like the person delivering it, or it may land flat on family members hearing it. It may not capture the deceased person well, either. Consider these kinds of effects as you read.
Strategic questions ask what to do. Should I take a daily aspirin? Should I buy the house? The answers combine information with judgment about goals, risks, trade-offs and personal circumstances.

My aspirin search shows why context matters. Google warned about risks, told me to consult a medical professional and offered more tailored information if I provided my age, cardiovascular history and risk of bleeding. That caution matches the US Preventive Services Task Force guidance. It says the decision to start low-dose aspirin for prevention of heart attacks and strokes should be individualized and weigh cardiovascular benefit against bleeding risk.

For strategic answers, ask what the system would need to know before its advice could reasonably apply to you individually. Consider the stakes, the alternatives and whether a qualified person should be involved. For the aspirin question, a useful follow-up would be: “What details about my age, medical history or bleeding risk could change this advice? What should I discuss with my doctor before deciding?” The final judgment remains yours because you are the person who has to live with the outcome.
My questions began as ordinary Google searches. I did not open a chatbot. The AI-generated responses simply arrived, and links were appended.

The responses were useful. Google added context, acknowledged complications and offered tailored guidance if I supplied additional information. Within each response, though, the type of answer could change. Reporting what a medical guideline says is different from deciding how it applies to a particular person. A fluent response can move between those types of answers without a noticeable change in voice.
As a user, try to recognize what kind of intellectual work the AI agent did for a response you receive. Consider whether the interpretation is persuasive or the advice fits your circumstances.
Before asking whether an AI answer is right, ask a more basic question: What kind of answer is this? The type will tell you what to do next. – Rappler.com
Leo S. Lo is a dean at the University of Virginia.

articles.title: Rapists could face life sentences and barristers prevented from ‘putting victims on trial’ under Victorian Labor reforms
articles.summary: Premier Ben Carroll says if re-elected Labor will legislate a new form of manslaughter and increase maximum penalty for rape to life imprisonment
articles.byline: Benita Kolovos and Australian Associated Press

blocks.text: Rapists could face life sentences and lawyers would be prevented from asking humiliating questions of victim-survivors under a suite of Victorian Labor pre-election commitments designed to reduce violence against women.

The premier, Ben Carroll, on Sunday announced an election commitment to legislate a new form of manslaughter covering cases in which a person takes their own life as a result of family violence, as well as a new offence covering perpetrators abandoning a victim in need of medical care.

The state government also plans to change the law to let courts consider patterns of sexual abuse as evidence at trial and stop barristers using “humiliating and invasive questioning techniques” in court.
“I’m sick of Victoria’s courts and defence barristers putting victims on trial,” Carroll told reporters on Sunday.
The maximum penalty for persistent family violence intervention order breaches would also be doubled to 10 years’ jail under Labor’s pitch.
The government said the two new offences would close “loopholes” that allow perpetrators to “slip through the cracks in the justice system and walk free”.

The government has also committed to increasing the maximum penalty for rape from 25 years to life imprisonment and upping the maximum penalty for every other serious sexual offence by five years. The maximum penalty for persistent breaches of family violence intervention orders would also double from five years’ imprisonment to 10.
It will also make the standard sentence for the murder of a current or former partner 30 years – up from 25.
The proposed offence criminalising the abandonment of victims in need of medical care responds to recommendations made by the coroner after the deaths of Belinda Jones and Narelle Simmons.

Jones, 40, died on the floor of her Maryborough home in July 2023 after her partner left her there overnight and then waited two hours to call an ambulance after waking to find her cold and not breathing.

Jones had succumbed to treatable bacterial infections and sepsis, which a hospital failed to diagnose during an emergency presentation days earlier. Her partner was not charged with any offence in relation to her death.

In her findings published last month, the state coroner, Liberty Sanger, said: “In my view, the act of abandoning a victim of family violence requiring medical attention is an act of family violence, that instils fear in the victim and affirms a perpetrator’s control over the victim.”
Simmons, 42, died in October 2021 after her partner admitted to punching her twice in the face and elbowing her once in the back of the head before leaving her Cranbourne home.
after newsletter promotion
Her body was found nine days later after her daughter requested a welfare check. Sanger was unable to determine whether she died immediately after the assault or hours or days later.

Her partner – whom the coroner said had 18 previous family violence victims – pleaded guilty to common assault and failing to report a reportable death. He was sentenced to five months’ imprisonment and a 12-month community corrections order.

The government’s announcement comes after a week of crime-focused election commitments from Carroll, including creating a new police training facility in Melbourne’s western suburbs and the introduction of Jack’s Law, which would give police and protective services officers the power to stop and search people for knives using handheld metal detectors.
“I’m a tough-on-crime premier – and that means being tough on family and sexual violence,” Carroll said in a statement before Sunday’s announcement.
“We must act on the violence that is killing a Victorian woman every two weeks.”

The Coalition last year committed to Jack’s Law and also have plans to expand adult sentencing for youth offenders, increase police numbers and split the existing court of appeal into two separate entities, if elected in November.

articles.title: [Just Saying] Phantom judges in the impeachment court
articles.summary: Constitutional provisions must never be fragmented and parsed into isolated words and phrases, each assigned a standalone meaning detached from the whole

blocks.text: Article XI Section 3(6) of the 1987 Constitution provides:

The Senate shall have the sole power to try and decide all cases of impeachment. When SITTING FOR THAT PURPOSE, the Senators shall be on OATH OR AFFIRMATION. When the President of the Philippines is on trial, the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court shall preside, but shall not vote. No person shall be convicted without the concurrence of two-thirds of ALL MEMBERS OF THE SENATE.

A senator does not automatically become an impeachment judge by virtue of holding legislative office. Section 3(6) mandates a structural metamorphosis: Senators become trial judges only when they take a separate oath or affirmation and officially convene by “sitting for that purpose” — specifically, “to try and decide.”

Therefore, the phrase “all the Members of the Senate” qualified to vote on conviction must refer exclusively to the pool of Senators who accomplish two elements: 1. Taking their oath and 2. actively sitting in the impeachment court. Both must concur. Non-accomplishment of one excludes a senator or a senator judge from “all members of the Senate.”

Because Section 3(6), Article XI of the 1987 Constitution was directly transplanted from prior constitutional texts, its construction does not depend on the speculative intent of the 1986 Framers, but on the plain, ordinary understanding of the People who ratified it. And even if there were deliberations regarding the provision, still the so-called intention of the framers must yield to the understanding of the people.

To the ratifying public, the choice of the word “sitting” in the phrase “sitting for that purpose” was not casual legalese; it is a deliberate, everyday term chosen because it naturally conveys a dual purpose:
The term “sitting for that purpose” seamlessly captures both the legal capacity and the physical act required of an impeachment adjudicator:
Capacity to Act as a Judge (De Jure Authority):

In popular understanding, a judge “sits” on the bench when invested with jurisdiction. When a senator takes the required special oath or affirmation, they undergo a constitutional metamorphosis — stripping off their pure legislative identity to assume the legal capacity of a judicial officer. “Sitting for that purpose” marks the assumption of this distinct judicial office.
Mandated Presence in Conducting the Trial (De Facto Exercise):

Simultaneously, “sitting” is a factual descriptor. An ordinary citizen understands that a court cannot “sit” in a vacuum. To be “sitting” means to be physically present, in the chair, actively conducting and hearing the proceedings. A judge who is absent is not “sitting.”

By fusing these two concepts into a single term easily understood by the public, the text establishes that legal capacity without physical presence does not constitute “sitting,” and therefore cannot qualify a Senator to be counted among the baseline of “all the Members of the Senate” who “try and decide” the case.
Simply, judicial power of a court which is a “trier of facts” which, in turn is the attribute of an impeachment court cannot be divorced from its exercise. And its exercise requires presence.
Historical perspective

Historically, Anglo-American trial tradition — from which this constitutional text was borrowed almost verbatim — treats a tribunal as a body that operates only when its members physically “sit” in court. To the public that ratified the Constitution, the term “sitting” carried the settled historical weight of court sessions: a tribunal “sits” when its judges gather in person to take evidence. The phrase was retained precisely because its historic, dual meaning — signifying both judicial session and physical attendance —was well established in public consciousness.
Constitutional perspective
Synthesizing the text, Section 3(6) creates a strict operational sequence:
1. The Oath/Affirmation: Grants the senator the capacity to act as a judge.
2. Sitting for the Purpose: Combines that judicial *capacity* with actual presence in the tribunal.
3. To Try and Decide: Dictates the action permitted only to those who are currently “sitting.”

If “all the Members of the Senate” were interpreted as a raw count of all elected legislators regardless of presence, the phrase “sitting for that purpose” would be rendered redundant surplusage. Constitutional interpretation dictates that every word must be given effect. “Sitting” qualifies the baseline of senators to only those who possess both the judicial capacity and the active presence during the trial.
Practical perspective

From a practical and common-sense perspective — the exact lens through which the ratifying public viewed the text — a person cannot “try” a case they did not watch or hear. The duty “to try” requires observing witnesses, evaluating demeanor, and weighing live evidence. The word “sitting” vividly communicates this physical necessity. The ordinary voter understood that you cannot judge a trial from afar; “sitting” requires being in the room where the trial takes place.
Political perspective

Politically, the double meaning of “sitting” prevents a grave constitutional abuse: the participation of “phantom judges.” If capacity alone were enough without mandated presence, politically aligned Senators could skip the trial, avoid hearing damaging evidence against an ally or opponent, and emerge at the final hour merely to vote. The requirement of “sitting” — meaning both holding the sworn capacity and maintaining actual presence — ensures that only those who endured the burden and public scrutiny of the bench are empowered to render judgment.

The ratifying people understood “sitting” in its common, intuitive sense. By retaining this exact word from previous Constitutions, the text enshrines a clear rule: to be counted among “all the Members of the Senate” who decide an impeachment, a senator must have taken the oath to gain the capacity of a judge, and must be actively present (“sitting”) in the trial court.

Constitutional provisions must never be fragmented and parsed into isolated words and phrases, each assigned a standalone meaning detached from the whole. A text adopted verbatim across generations must be construed as an integrated, seamless structure, interpreted continuously in the light of the Constitution’s enduring principles — chiefly due process, which demands that those who decide must actually hear the evidence, and participatory democracy, which requires active, transparent, and accountable engagement rather than passive partisan head counts.

It is entirely understandable that the ouster of a high official elected by the sovereign people should carry a heavy measure of difficulty. However, difficulty must never be equated with absurdity. The claim advanced by some sectors — that fixing the two-thirds threshold to an inflexible 16 senator-judges saves the impeachment process from political manipulation — may sound superficially plausible. Yet, if applied, forcing such a rigid number regardless of how many senators actually qualify, take the oath, and sit for the trial produces an irrational implementation that is far more destructive of the constitutional process itself.

Isolating the phrase “all the Members of the Senate” from its constitutional anchors — “sitting for that purpose” and the requirement of a distinct oath — shatters this holistic design. Departing from these fundamental rules of interpretation produces an obviously absurd result: an impeachment court where non-attending, unsworn, or non-participating legislators can decide the fate of a trial they never witnessed. Such an outcome subverts the foundational guarantees of judicial fairness and democratically accountable governance, yielding a practical impossibility that only a clever manipulation of semantics can ostensibly justify. – Rappler.com

Mel Sta. Maria is former dean of the Far Eastern University Institute of Law. He teaches law at FEU, the Ateneo School of Law, the University of Sto. Tomas, Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila, University of Makati, and Manuel L. Quezon University. He also hosts shows on both radio and YouTube, and has authored several books on law, politics, and current events.

articles.title: Germany: Is it possible to replace the chancellor?
articles.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz's record-low approval ratings have emboldened his opponents. There are three ways to remove a chancellor from office in Germany.

image.caption: Sixteen months into office, Friedrich Merz has record low approval ratings, triggering a debate abour his futureImage: Annegret Hilse/REUTERS

blocks.text: It is the hot topic this week in Berlin: Does German Chancellor Friedrich Merz still have the backing of his own party, the Christian Democrats (CDU), and the coalition partners, Bavaria's Christian Social Union (CSU) and the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD)? Will he be ousted? How would that work? Can he just step down?

Support for the chancellor has reached a record low: In the latest Deutschlandtrend representative survey, conducted by pollsters Infratest-Dimap for German public broadcaster ARD in early September, only 13% of respondents said Merz was doing a good job.
In early September, Merz's CDU suffered a resounding loss in the state of Saxony-Anhalt's parliamentary election, seeing the party's result halved from the 2021 election.
The election result has reinforced criticism of Merz, even from within his own ranks, and his communication style, which frequently alienates his audience.
But Merz remains chancellor. What are the options to change that? Germany's constitution, the Basic Law, grants the position a strong standing. German chancellors are not so easy to unseat.
Option 1: Resignation

Merz himself can decide to resign for any reason. That would not necessarily mean the end of the coalition government he leads. An example: In May 1974, then Chancellor Willy Brandt of the SPD resigned after a spy from communist East Germany (DDR) was discovered to have been working in his inner circle. The governing parties, the SPD and the business-oriented Free Democrats (FDP), quickly agreed to continue their alliance.

Only 10 days later, Finance Minister Helmut Schmidt, also of the SPD, was elected as the new chancellor. To do this, an absolute majority of all lawmakers in the Bundestag, the lower house of parliament, was needed (not only those present during the vote). This majority is called the "chancellor majority". Schmidt achieved the necessary majority, eventually got reelected and remained head of the German government for 8 years.
How likely is Merz to step down? Today's chancellor seems determined not to give up.
Option 2: A constructive vote of no-confidence

If a new majority were formed through alliances in the Bundestag or if a chancellor fell so far out of favor that their own supporters no longer believed in them, the instrument of a "constructive vote of no-confidence" could come into play. That means the majority of lawmakers vote in favor of a new candidate for chancellor.

An example: Helmut Schmidt of the SPD, lost the support of his junior coalition partner, the FDP, in 1982. The FDP wanted to push through changes to economic policy, which Schmidt rejected. They joined forces with the conservatives from the CDU and CSU, and jointly put CDU leader Helmut Kohl forward as a new chancellor. He won a majority in parliament, replaced Schmidt and moved into the chancellor's office where he remained for 16 years.

The probability of this happening in Merz's case is very remote. The conservatives and Social Democrats do not want to end their coalition. There is no clear rival candidate for Merz. North Rhine-Westphalia's State Premier Hendrik Wüst of the CDU is seen as a possible successor, but has not made a step forward. Besides: The CDU is usually very loyal toward its political leaders; ousting the chancellor via a vote of no-confidence on the open stage of the Bundestag is simply unthinkable for most conservative lawmakers.
Option 3: A confidence vote

Germany's parliament cannot simply dissolve itself and call new elections. Lawmakers can, however, call a confidence vote on the chancellor and his government. Several chancellors have already used this mechanism, coupling it with a vote on a contentious issue.

As chancellor in November 2001, Gerhard Schröder (SPD) put forward a confidence vote in the Bundestag and linked it with the question of whether his government should deploy the German military to Afghanistan to support the NATO mission led by the United States following the September 11 attacks. Schröder won, remained in office and continued with his military policy.
Merz has already said he sees no point in calling for a confidence vote. There are also no signs of large breakaway movements from members of his coalition in Parliament.

If a chancellor loses a confidence vote, the Bundestag can be dissolved and fresh elections called. Following the defeat in the Bundestag, the chancellor can ask the German President to dissolve parliament and call voters to the polls. The president is not obliged to do so, but usually does.
It seems that Merz has ruled out this option. Neither the SPD nor the conservative Union (of CDU/CSU) are interested in calling new elections at a time when their approval ratings are low.
So will the government remain the same? Right now, it seems so. However, things have been so dynamic in recent days and weeks in Berlin political circles that nothing should be ruled out.
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: One child dead and two children and woman in critical condition after Blue Mountains stabbing
articles.summary: Crime scene established at Waratah Road, Valley Heights as NSW police say they ‘are not looking for any other people at this time’

blocks.text: A child has died in a stabbing attack in the Blue Mountains, with two other children and a woman in hospital in critical condition, New South Wales police say.
In a statement on Sunday afternoon, police said emergency services responded to reports of three children and a woman with stab wounds in a vehicle on Waratah Road, Valley Heights.

“Officers from Blue Mountains Police Area Command have been informed that several members of the public performed first aid on the woman and three children whilst contacting Triple Zero,” they said in a statement.
One of the children was located deceased in the vehicle.

Police said NSW Ambulance treated the two children, who are believed to be under five, and the woman, believed to be in her 40s, at the scene before they were taken to Westmead hospital, where all three are listed as being in a critical condition.
“A crime scene has been established, and police are not looking for any other people at this time,” they said.
Police are urging anyone with information or mobile phone or dashcam footage of the incident to contact Crime Stoppers.

articles.title: Two killed in 'massive' Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow region, says Russia
articles.summary: An oil refinery was also reportedly hit in Moscow, and flights were suspended at two capital airports.

blocks.text: At least two people have been killed and six injured in a "massive" overnight Ukrainian drone attack on the Moscow region, Governor Andrei Vorobyev has said.

Vorobyev said 249 drones had been shot down, and he reported fires in several residential houses. A local warehouse was also ablaze. In the capital Moscow, an oil refinery was damaged, and flight restrictions were in place at two airports.
Earlier, a Ukraine official said seven people, including two children, were killed in Russian attacks in the Kyiv and Sumy regions on Saturday.
Russia and Ukraine have recently intensified their strikes, targeting energy-generating and transport facilities, as well as major logistics hubs.

In a post on Telegram on Sunday, Vorobyev said a 44-year-old woman was killed in Sofyino after a drone hit a three-storey residential building. Another five people - including two children - were injured, he said.
In the Orekhovo-Zuevo district, an elderly man died after a private house was hit, the regional governor said.
Videos have emerged on social media purportedly showing explosions in the night skies in the Moscow region, and of a burning warehouse. The footage has not been verified by the BBC.
Meanwhile, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said a drone struck a building near one of the capital's boulevards and a facility at an oil refinery was damaged.
He earlier said that 152 drones heading for Moscow had been shot down.
Sheremetyevo - Moscow's biggest airport - warned passengers about "temporary restrictions" in place, while at the capital's Vnukovo airport all arrivals and departures were halted.
In Ukraine, a mother and her two small children, a boy and a girl, were killed in Saturday's Russian attack in the city of Fastiv, Kyiv regional head Tymur Tkachenko said.
He added that several private houses were also damaged.
In the north-eastern Sumy region, four people were killed when a Russian drone hit the car they were travelling in, top local official Oleh Hryhorov said.
Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

articles.title: PH earns first 2026 Asian Games medal with historic bronze in soft tennis
articles.summary: The quintet of Bien Zoleta, Princess Catindig, Hilary Paas, Shyryn Salazar, and Christy Sañosa make history as the Philippines secures its first-ever podium finish in Asian Games soft tennis

blocks.text: MEDALISTS. The Philippine women's tennis team of (from left) Hilary Paas, Princess Catindig, Bien Zoleta, Christy Sañosa, Shyryn Salazar deliver in the 2026 Asian Games.
Bien Zoleta Facebook page
The quintet of Bien Zoleta, Princess Catindig, Hilary Paas, Shyryn Salazar, and Christy Sañosa make history as the Philippines secures its first-ever podium finish in Asian Games soft tennis
MANILA, Philippines – It did not take long for the Philippines to break the medal ice at the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan.

Less than 24 hours after the opening ceremony, the country won its first medal courtesy of the women’s soft tennis team, which bagged a bronze despite its 2-0 loss to defending champion Japan in the semifinals at the Higashiyama Park Tennis Center on Sunday, September 20.

Aside from delivering the Philippines’ maiden medal in this edition of the continental showpiece, the quintet of Bien Zoleta, Princess Catindig, Hilary Paas, Shyryn Salazar, and Christy Sañosa made history as the country secured its first podium finish in Asian Games soft tennis.

“It’s such an overwhelming feeling because this isn’t just for us, it’s for the Philippines, especially knowing that we’re the first ones to get a medal. We hope this can boost the morale of other national athletes who will be competing in the coming days,” Zoleta told reporters in a mix of Filipino and English.
“We really worked to win this, especially here in the Asian Games. For us in soft tennis, this is our Olympics. So to win a medal here means so much to us.”
The Philippines started its campaign with a 3-0 win over Mongolia and a 2-1 victory over Thailand.
Although it wrapped up the preliminary round with a 0-3 loss to Chinese Taipei, the Philippines still earned a top-two finish in Group B to advance to the semifinals and assure itself of a medal.
In the semifinals, Japan — which ruled the women’s team event in three of the last four editions, including the last two — displayed its dominance.

Zoleta and Catindig absorbed a 5-0 loss to Rena Temma and Kiho Miyamae in the opening doubles match before Sañosa fell to Ayaka Iwakura, 4-0, in singles play, paving the way for Japan to return to the finals.
But the defeat did little to wipe the smiles off the Filipinas’ faces as the country finally broke through in a sport that made its Asian Games debut in 1994.
“We are very, very proud and very, very happy to win a medal for the country,” said Zoleta. – Rappler.com

articles.summary: Several groups convened at EDSA Shrine on Sunday as they continue to seek accountability from those involved in corruption, just a day before the 54th commemoration of the Martial Law declaration.

blocks.text: Published September 20, 2026 12:28pm
Several groups convened at EDSA Shrine on Sunday as they continue to seek accountability from those involved in corruption, just a day before the 54th commemoration of the Martial Law declaration.

Before proceeding to EDSA Shrine, civil society group August Twenty One Movement first held a motorcade in the morning going to the Supreme Court (SC) in Manila to air their grievances over the recent acquittal of former First Lady Imelda Romualdez Marcos of graft charges.

The SC recently overturned Imelda's graft conviction over her alleged financial interests in seven Swiss foundations, after finding the prosecution’s testimonial and documentary evidence inadmissible and lacking in probative value.

On the other hand, there were also groups who marched from the House of Representatives in Quezon City to EDSA Shrine. They are protesting against anomalous flood control projects in the country. The groups are also calling for an end to job contractualization and political dynasty.
Likewise, a group of students gathered at La Salle Greenhills in Mandaluyong City to proceed to EDSA Shrine and call for accountability on the flood control scandal.

Over 15,000 cops from the National Capital Region Police Office and nearby regions have been deployed since Saturday evening in preparation for the upcoming 54th Martial Law commemoration. —Vince Angelo Ferreras/KG, GMA News

The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) Electronic Support System (LESS) is currently offline as the agency investigates a reported security breach.
LESS is LTFRB's digital platform used to process online applications, handle transactions, and provide electronic support to motorists.
"Dahil dito, suspendido muna hanggang sa susunod na abiso ang lahat ng serbisyo at transaksyong may kaugnayan sa LESS," LTFRB said in a statement on Saturday.

"Pinapayuhan ang lahat ng concerned offices at personnel na huwag munang mag-access o magproseso ng anumang transaksyon sa pamamagitan ng LESS hanggang sa mailabas ang opisyal na abiso hinggil sa pagpapanumbalik ng sistema," it added.
(All concerned offices and personnel are advised not to access or process any transactions through LESS until an official notice is issued regarding the restoration of the system.)
LTFRB further said it is coordinating with the Communications Technology (DICT) and Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) in investigating the incident.
The LTFRB is also coordinating with the National Privacy Commission (NPC) in validating the specific data affected by the incident.
"Tinitiyak ng LTFRB sa publiko na agad na ipinatutupad ang lahat ng kinakailangang data security measures upang matugunan ang insidente sa lalong madaling panahon," LTFRB said.

articles.title: LTFRB to submit fare hike recommendation to DOTr by October
articles.summary: The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board on Sunday said that its recommendation on the fare hike is expected to be submitted to the Department of Transportation in October.

blocks.text: Published September 20, 2026 10:48am
The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) on Sunday said that its recommendation on the fare hike is expected to be submitted to the Department of Transportation in October.
LTFRB acting chairman Atty. Greg Pua Jr. said the agency is currently finalizing its recommendation, taking into consideration the expected increase in oil prices.
"Ang utos sa amin, by October, dapat nasa kanyang table na ang [recommendation] for approval," Pua told Super Radyo dzBB.
(The order is for us to submit [to Department of Transportation Secretary Giovanni Lopez] the recommendation for approval by October.)
"Once he [makes the decision], we will immediately implement whatever increase we will implement," he added.

Another big-time increase in fuel products is expected this week due to the Middle East fuel crisis, with diesel prices possibly surging by over P10 per liter and gasoline prices increasing by as high as P5 per liter. An industry source on Saturday said diesel prices may go up by P8.50 to P9.50 per liter and gasoline by P4.50 to P5.50 per liter.
Diesel and gas prices have gone up by P10/L in the past two weeks.

Lopez earlier this week said he gave LTFRB enough time to weigh all the factors, adding that DOTr will check the initiatives that the government is already rolling out to public utility vehicle (PUV) drivers.

“At the end of the day, ang talagang utos ng Pangulo is as much as possible, hindi dapat binibigay sa mga commuters natin or pinapasa sa commuters natin ‘yung problemang ito. Kailangan saluhin ho ng gobyerno at kailangan saluhin ng Department of Transportation,” Lopez said.

(At the end of the day, the President has ordered that as much as possible, the problem should not be passed on to the commuters. It should be shouldered by the government and the Department of Transportation.)
Fuel subsidy

Meanwhile, the LTFRB has suspended the distribution of the P12-per-liter fuel subsidy for PUV drivers due to the election ban on public spending for social services ahead of the upcoming Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE).
The LTRFB is currently waiting for the Commission on Elections' (Comelec) approval on its certificate of exemption to provide financial assistance to public utility vehicle (PUV) drivers.

"As early as Tuesday last week, sumulat na tayo sa Comelec in anticipation dito sa election ban. Sumulat na tayo sa Comelec na ma-exempt tayo sa mga programa ng LTFRB, 'yung financial assistance at P12 discount," Pua said

(As early as Tuesday last week, we had already written to the Commission on Election in anticipation of the election ban. We asked Comelec to exempt from the ban the LTFRB’s programs, particularly the financial assistance and the P12 discount.)
"We are waiting sa approval ng Comelec, which we hope na matanggap namin (we receive it) this coming week," he added.

During election period, a certificate of exemption is given to a government agency to allow specific activities that fall under the elections ban, like releasing or disbursing public funds for social welfare, housing, or infrastructure projects and transporting firearms.
The release, disbursement, or expenditure of public funds is prohibited from September 18 to November 1 due to the upcoming BSKE scheduled for November 2. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: CICC asks IT communities to help gov't vs school violence
articles.summary: The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) on Sunday asked IT communities to "come forward" and help the government amid the recent incident of school violence in South Cotabato that…

blocks.text: Published September 20, 2026 10:20am

The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) on Sunday asked IT communities to "come forward" and help the government amid the recent incident of school violence in South Cotabato that is being linked to the dark web.

"Sa ating mga kapatid, sa ating mga kasamahan, sa ating mga kaibigan sa mga iba't-ibang mga ICT communities, hacking communities, computer forums, kung may alam kayo or may access dito, mag-come forward kayo," said CICC executive director Aboy Paraiso in an interview with Super Radyo dzBB.

(To our brothers and sisters, to our colleagues, to our friends in various ICT communities, hacking communities, and computer forums, if you know anything or have access to this, please come forward.)

"Hindi na ito usapin ng i-correct niyo kami sa gobyerno, aminado kami na tayo na may kakulangan tayo sa pamahalaan, at kayo ho ang magpupuno ng mga kaalaman na 'yun," he added. "Magtulong-tulong tayo para sa ating mga kabataan. Please come forward. We don't need another incident like this, not at the expense of another child's life."
The Department of the Interior and Local Government earlier said that the shooter at Banga National High School was heavily into the dark web.
The police, on the other hand, said that the shooter was into online activities "showing violent activities."
According to CICC, the deep web is beyond what we can publicly access on the internet as it requires special software and even skills to get into it.
The dark web is mostly linked to illegal activities.

"These are the websites na wala sa mga browsers natin. Kailangan natin mag-access nito through some other forms of applications or systems, para ma-access natin ito. Kung saan naman mga iba't-ibang mga impormasyon, whether nagu-usap yung mga nasa hacking community, the illegal sales of illegal firearms, yung mga community na ayaw magpakilala or nagtatago, nandito sa forums na ito," said Paraiso.

(These are the websites that aren't available on our standard browsers. We need to access this through some other forms of applications or systems to get in. In these forums, you can find various kinds of information, whether it's people in the hacking community talking, the sale of illegal firearms, or communities that want to remain anonymous or hide.)
The CICC advised parents to monitor their children's online activities.

"You better think again na parang anyone is being targeted right now. Kapag naging distant na yung mga anak niyo or medyo iritable na dahil may kausap silang iba, ibig sabihin napalitan na kayo bilang magulang," said Paraiso.

(You better think again, as anyone can be targeted right now. When your children become distant or somewhat irritable because they are talking to someone else, it means you have already been replaced as a parent.) —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Future of German chancellor hangs in the balance as two states go to polls
articles.summary:
Embattled Friedrich Merz faces nervous wait while far-right Alternative für Deutschland party targets further gains

Voters in two German states are going to the polls with the political…

blocks.text: Voters in two German states are going to the polls with the political future of the embattled chancellor, Friedrich Merz, hanging in the balance and an emboldened far right targeting further gains.

Coming two weeks after a seismic election in Saxony-Anhalt in which the anti-immigration, pro-Kremlin Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) scored its highest ever result in a regional poll, the nativist party is expected to drain support again from Merz’s conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU).

Just how brutal the outcome is could affect Merz’s ability to hang on as leader after only 16 months in power, possibly setting wheels in motion for his replacement or even snap elections – currently regarded as unlikely but not ruled out.

blocks.caption: A campaign poster for Kristin Brinker and Julian Adrat, candidates of the AfD, in Berlin.   Photograph: Liesa Johannssen/Reuters

blocks.text: About 2.5 million people are eligible to vote in the capital Berlin and nearly 1.3 million in the Baltic coast state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Polling booths open at 8am local time on Sunday and will close at 6pm, when Merz and his allies will be watching exit polls on tenterhooks.
The luckless chancellor has resisted calls to quit and vowed to fight for a signature package of economic and social welfare changes he argues are crucial to Germany’s future.
“We as a government were elected for four years, I was elected for four years,” he told an industry group. “And I want to use these four years to lead the country out of this difficult period.”

Merz, whose personal approval ratings have nosedived to 10%, cancelled a plan to speak at the UN general assembly in New York because “his presence is required in Berlin” after the elections, a government official said.

His credibility has been tarnished by broken campaign promises to return Europe’s largest economy to growth and cut the AfD, the biggest opposition party in parliament and number one in opinion polls, down to size.

blocks.caption: Protesters attend a demonstration against the AfD in Berlin earlier this week. Photograph: Liesa Johannssen/Reuters

blocks.text: The AfD fell just short of an absolute majority in former communist Saxony-Anhalt, which would have allowed it to govern on its own. It is looking for defectors from other parties to make it the first far-right force to run a German state since the Nazi period.
However, polls indicate the AfD will fall well short of such a prospect in both of Sunday’s elections, even with its palpable sense of momentum.

In Berlin, which is one of Germany’s 16 federal states, the incumbent CDU is vying for first place against the far-left Die Linke, which has called for expropriation of corporate landlords to fight rising housing costs.
About 85% of Berlin households rent their ​homes and advertised rents have nearly doubled since 2014, when the city was still labelled “poor but sexy” by its then mayor, Klaus Wowereit.
The AfD is polling strongly in third or fourth place, even in the cosmopolitan capital.

The current mayor, Kai Wegner of the CDU, abandoned his re-election bid in July after getting tangled in contradictions explaining a decision to play tennis while large parts of the German capital were hit by an arson-triggered power blackout last winter.
Stefan Evers, Berlin’s chief finance official, replaced him as the candidate but has failed to lift the party’s polling scores.

blocks.caption: Campaign posters for the Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania state elections in Schwerin, Germany. Photograph: Annegret Hilse/Reuters

blocks.text: In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the situation looks even dicier for Merz, whose weakness regional leaders have blamed for their poor showing. The AfD and the Social Democrats are locked in a neck-and-neck race while the CDU risks its first single-digit result in 75 years.
If it crashes out of parliament entirely by falling below the 5% bar to representation, it would be unprecedented in the postwar period and mark a stinging setback for Merz’s quest to stay in office.

The AfD’s triumph in Saxony-Anhalt sent shock waves through Germany and beyond and has left Merz’s back to the wall, with speculation rampant he could be replaced by another Christian Democrat as chancellor well before the next general election, due in 2029.
Holger Schmieding, the chief economist at Berenberg bank, said he still expected Merz to serve out his full term.

“But the risk that the CDU may revolt against him and replace the unpopular chancellor seems to have risen from 20% 10 days ago to roughly 35% now, in my view,” he said in a research note, underlining the impact of a global rise in petrol prices on already angry voters.

Although some economic indicators have improved on Merz’s watch, soaring living costs and deindustrialisation in core sectors such as automaking in the face of Chinese competition have taken a heavy toll.

Meanwhile a significant reduction in new arrivals at the border has failed to win back AfD voters, who are responding to the party’s strong focus on economic anxiety, fears around crime, and resistance to Merz’s staunch support for Ukraine.
The AfD built its victory in Saxony-Anhalt in large part by mobilising non-voters.

Its opponents are hoping the spectre of a far-right juggernaut across Germany will get voters to the polls in support of mainstream democratic parties, after tens of thousands joined anti-AfD street protests in the wake of the Saxony-Anhalt rout.

articles.title: Man charged with stabbing murder of 90-year-old woman in Bondi Beach amid spate of alleged domestic violence killings
articles.summary: Three women were killed in separate incidents just hours apart in NSW on Saturday
articles.byline: Australian Associated Press and Guardian staff

blocks.text: Three women have died just hours apart in separate incidents in one state, including an elderly woman who was fatally stabbed in an alleged domestic violence attack.
A 47-year-old man has been charged with murder after the woman in her 90s was found with stab wounds inside her unit at Sydney’s Bondi Beach at about 5.15pm on Saturday.
The woman was treated by paramedics but died at the scene.
Police established a crime scene not far from the famous beach as detectives began investigating the circumstances.
The man will appear before a bail court on Sunday.
Just hours after the death, the body of another woman in her 70s was found at Mole River in the state’s north.
Police were called to reports of a domestic violence incident in the regional district about 9.35pm.
Investigators believe a 37-year-old man entered a property and tried to steal a vehicle before assaulting the 74-year-old resident.
The younger man was arrested and police then went on to search the neighbouring property where they found the body of a woman in her 70s, who is yet to be formally identified.
Part of the house was damaged by fire, police said.
A crime scene has been established at both locations and an investigation launched with help from the homicide squad.
Earlier on Saturday, a 23-year-old woman was found with critical stab wounds inside a home in Wagga Wagga, in south-western NSW.
Emergency services were called to the home about 11.45am but the woman died at the scene.
Police were told a man left the location before officers arrived.
An 18-year-old man was arrested at the scene and taken to Wagga Wagga police station, but he was later released without charge.
About 8.30pm, a 31-year-old man was arrested at a home and taken to Wagga Wagga police station, where he remains.
All three people are believed to have known each other.
In a statement, the NSW opposition leader, Kellie Sloane, said she was “horrified by the alleged stabbing deaths”.

“These deaths are not isolated. According to the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, a woman was killed every 11 days in 2024-25 by her intimate partner. Even more women lose their lives when you include other family members,” she said.
“Women of every age, from a 23-year-old to a woman in her 90s, are still not safe in their own homes.

“Because these matters are before the courts, I won’t comment on the circumstances. But we cannot treat this as background noise. We are failing women across our country and every level of government, and every one of us, has a responsibility to act.”

articles.title: Ed Sheeran addresses Macklemore controversy at Philadelphia show
articles.summary: The mega-star singer held his first concert since rapper Macklemore was removed from his tour and other artists dropped out.

blocks.text: Singer Ed Sheeran opened his latest concert alone onstage and apologised to his fans for making "mistakes" as he handled the fallout from the controversy over American rapper Macklemore being dropped from his tour over pro-Palestinian remarks.
"I never wanted to be an activist musician but this has put me in the middle of an important and passionate argument about free speech and the most complex political issue on the planet," he said.
Saturday's show at a Philadelphia sports stadium was the first time he has addressed the matter in person.
It was a stripped down event and Sheeran went on without opening acts after several musicians dropped out over the debacle.
The price for tickets dropped and sales declined for the remaining US leg of his Loop Tour due to the controversy.
The singer has said the decision to drop Macklemore was made by his promoters, not him.
"My concerts have always been a safe space for everyone," he said at the start of the show, adding that he is committed to fans and that is why he returned to the stage.
"Now, I want to address the question of where I stand in the situation in Israel and Palestine, and whether my doing this concert here tonight implies where I stand," he said.

"I have tried in my career not to be a political commentator of any kind, because I want my music and shows to be about unity, not division; about humanity, not politics. But this is a humanitarian issue, and I cannot hide how I feel about it anymore."
Sheeran said what happened in Israel during the 7 October 2023 attacks was "horrific and compounded centuries of Jewish pain".

He added: "What is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate. My heart has been broken by the scale of of devastation and loss of civilian lives, of children's lives, and this systemic injustice we're seeing unfold in the West Bank cannot be overlooked."
He said he is trying "to work out how to make a contribution that helps victims of these terrible times and listening and learning, because I do not know enough".

Sheeran's remaining tour dates are scheduled with shows set throughout North and South America. While the mega-star's previous tour was among the highest-grossing of all time, some ticket prices for this show have dropped to $32 (£24).
Fans also reported being able to get ticket refunds, though Ticketmaster and concert promoter Messina Touring Group did not confirm they were being reimbursed.
An hour or so before the show began, hundreds concert-goers began to stream in for the event.
There was a smattering of press cameras outside the entry gates, though most fans skipped talking to the press.
A few dozen protesters turned up outside the nearest tube stop waving flags as ticket holders streamed towards Lincoln Financial Field - but the concert proceeded largely unfettered.
Of the handful of attendees who stopped to talk to the BBC, there was a sentiment of determination to enjoy an evening of music while at the same time supporting freedom of speech.
One married couple, who paid $450 per ticket, said that they respect Macklemore's right to speak freely.
Another group of two ladies, who told us they got a "deal" for tonight's concert after prices dropped, said that they support a free Palestine and at the same time love Sheeran's music.
Finally, one family let their two young teenage daughters, Victoria, 15 and Sadie,13 be interviewed.
When we asked what they thought of the controversy and Macklemore's removal, they replied "Who is Macklemore?".
